AI Hub

Everyone is confused. That is the honest starting line.

AI is on the billboards, in the all-hands, and in nobody's training budget. This is a calm place to build the basics — and then learn the part almost no one teaches: how to check what the AI gives you, instead of trusting it.

Show me where to start I already use AI — teach me to verify it

Free. No sign-up, no account, nothing to install. Works on a phone.

The problem, named

You are not behind. The ground is genuinely unclear.

This hub was built from one page of notes about what actually makes AI confusing right now. Six problems came out of it. If any of these are yours, you are in the right place — and you are in very ordinary company.

01

Noise everywhere, training nowhere

AI is on the news, in podcasts, on cars, trains and billboards, and in every company all-hands. Employers say "embrace AI to improve productivity" — and then run no formal training at all.

02

Too many teachers, no way to grade them

YouTube and Instagram are full of AI tutorials. Some are good. Some are vague. Some are too simple to use, some too deep to follow. Nothing tells you which is which before you've wasted the hour.

03

Too many models, no idea which is right

New names every month, each claiming to be the best. Several look free — until you hit a limit nobody explained. Choosing feels like a bet you're not qualified to place.

04

The mental model is usually wrong

Almost nobody was handed a working picture of what this thing is. So people reasonably guess: that it's a better search engine, that someone is answering, or — because it's warm and remembers what you just said — that it's something like a friend. Every one of those guesses is sensible. Each one quietly produces a different bad habit.

05

No way to check the answer

This is the big one. Nobody teaches how to validate what an AI produces. Blind trust isn't leverage — it's a risk you can't see. An answer you can't check is not an answer you can use.

06

Same starting line, no visible line

Nobody has twenty years of experience with this, which is a fairer start than most technologies offer — young or old, technical or not. It is not a level field: money, hardware and language still tilt it. But the gap is months of practice, not a degree. And a fair start is useless if nobody can find the start. Most people are shooting in the dark.

Why this hub exists

Every section below exists to close one of those six gaps. Nothing here needs any technical background, and everything here is meant to be tested against your own experience rather than believed — including the claims on this page.

Before anything else

The 60-second version

Six true things. If you only ever read one screen of this hub, read this one.

  1. No human is typing the reply.

    It is a program running in a data centre. It gives different answers to the same question because a little randomness is built in on purpose — not because you got a different person. But "no one is typing" is not "no one can ever see it": conversations can be stored, sampled by staff reviewing safety, or read by your employer if the account is company-issued. What that means for you is on the Trust page.

  2. It is not a search engine.

    Search finds pages that someone already wrote. An AI chatbot composes an answer word by word instead of retrieving one. Usually the result is new; sometimes it reproduces wording it was trained on. Either way nobody checked it before it reached you — which is why it can be brilliant, and why it can be confidently, fluently wrong.

  3. It predicts language. It does not "know" things.

    It was trained on an enormous amount of writing and learned which words tend to follow which. Being right is usually a side effect of that. It is never a guarantee.

    It is then trained a second time on human ratings of its answers. That is what makes it helpful and polite — and also what makes it inclined to agree with you.

  4. It sounds equally confident whether it is right or wrong.

    There is no wobble in its voice when it invents something. Confidence carries no information. This single fact is why the Trust track exists.

  5. It is not a companion, even when it feels like one.

    The warmth is a property of the text, not of a mind that cares about you. It has no stake in your life, and no memory of you unless the product was built to keep one. It can still be genuinely useful — just don't mistake the feeling for a relationship.

  6. The skill is not "prompting". It is judgement.

    The people getting real value are not the ones with magic words. They are the ones who know what to ask for, and can tell a good answer from a plausible one.

The six tracks

Pick where you are. Nothing here has to be done in order.

Each track is one page. Each page is skimmable in five minutes and expandable when you want the detail.

Track 0 · Foundations

What AI actually is

 Track 1 · The Map

What you don't know you don't know

You cannot ask for help you can't imagine. A map of what AI is genuinely good at, genuinely bad at, and unpredictable at — plus five habits for finding the gaps yourself.

 Track 2 · Trust

How to check the AI's work

The core of the hub. Six verification moves, a triage rule for how hard to check, the failure modes to recognise on sight, and a one-page checklist you can keep.

 Track 3 · Leverage

How to actually get help from it

The mental model that works, the five parts of a good request, ten patterns worth stealing, the beginner mistakes that waste the most time, and the three levels of tool most people never move past.

 Track 4 · Tools

Which model, and what "free" means

Stop trying to memorise the leaderboard. Learn the six categories of tool, a decision flow for picking one, why free tiers end, and how to run your own five-prompt test.

Study, work, and building something

A four-week plan at 20 minutes a day. How to find AI-shaped work in your job. What this does to careers, honestly. And what it really takes to start an AI company.

Ground rules

What this is, and what it isn't

What it is

  • Plain language. No jargon without a translation.
  • Free, with no account and nothing to install.
  • Honest about what nobody knows yet.
  • Focused on judgement, not tricks.

What it isn't

  • Not a certificate, a course, or a funnel.
  • Not sponsored by, or ranking, any AI company. Nothing here is paid for or affiliated.
  • Not a live leaderboard — model names age in weeks.
  • Not a substitute for a doctor, lawyer, or accountant.
Read this page the way it teaches you to read AI

This hub was written on 5 August 2026. The ideas here are durable; specific product names, prices and limits are not, and are deliberately kept out of it. Where a fact could go stale, the page says so instead of pretending. If something here contradicts what you can verify yourself today — trust what you verified.
